newsitem.title: USA: Quality Dining ex-directors weigh options for firm.
newsitem.headline: Quality Dining ex-directors weigh options for firm.

text.p: Two former directors of Quality Dining Inc said they hired an investment banking firm to consider options for the company, which last year bought the bagel chain they founded.
In a Securities and Exchange Commission filing, Nordahl Brue and Michael Dressell, who resigned from the board last month, raised concern over operation of the company.

"...(M)anagement of the company does not have a viable plan to grow, or to finance the growth of, its business as owner, operator and franchisor of Bruegger's Bagel Bakery...," Brue and Dressell said in the SEC filing made this week.
Neither Brue nor Dressell, who were founders of Bruegger's, were immediately available for comment.
Brue holds 2,149,625 shares of Quality Dining and Dressell owns 2,163,701, according to the filing, accounting together for 25.5 percent of Quality Dining's shares outstanding.
They also operate more than 150 Bruegger's restaurants as the company's largest franchisee.

In the filing, the men said they hired the investment banking firm of Gleacher Natwest Inc to consider options for Quality Dining, including separating the bagel chain from its other restaurant operations.

In a statement, Quality Dining said it was disappointed that Brue and Dressell "apparently disagree with the comprehensive strategic business plan which has been approved and adopted by the company's board of directors and management."

Brue and Dressell said in the filing no decision has been made as yet on what actions should be taken to maximize the value of the stock. Quality Dining shares on Wednesday were off 3/8 at 13-1/2, which compares with a 52-week high of 39-1/2 and a 52-week low of 10-1/2.

In the filing, Brue and Dressell said they are considering nominating three directors at Quality Dining's annual meeting, which is scheduled to be held March 26. Three current directors of the company are slated for reelection.
In its statement, Quality Dining said it was surprised that Brue and Dressell may propose nominees for the board "in light of their resignations from the board only last month."
When they resigned from Quality Dining's board last month, the two men said they wanted to focus on other business interests, including their Bruegger's franchises.
A Quality Dining spokesman was not immediately available for further comment.
Quality Dining said it has many initiatives underway in all of its restaurant concepts, including Bruegger's, which are designed to grow the business and enhance shareholder value.

Quality Dining's other restaurant concepts include Grady's American Grill, Spageddies Italian Kitchen and Papa Vino's Italian Kitchen. It also operates Burger King and Chili's Grill & Bar restaurants as a franchisee.
